script: Woman takes revenge against car dealership. I was just a month into driving my new car when the dealership came to repossess it. Their guys pulled up in a squad car, brand‑new tires, and I was left standing in the parking lot with my hands in my pockets, like, "What the actual heck?" (I know, right?) Then I started digging into the legal side. I pulled up the Ohio Secretary of State's database, and I found the dealer hadn't renewed their registration under their company name. I literally thought, "Wow, they're that sloppy." But here's the thing: I could register the dealership's name in my own name. I did it. I was like, "You're not getting away with this." (Honestly, that felt like a power move.) I drafted a cease‑and‑desist, sent it straight to their legal team, and told them to stop using the name they'd been flaunting since 2012. I hit them with a deadline, a threat of litigation, and a reminder that they're a buy‑here‑pay‑here place that masquerades as a legit dealership. (Karmic irony, am I right?) I know the dealership's reputation: they're sued a lot—73 cases on the Lima municipal court site. They're the type that loves to sue, and now they're losing business name registration. I felt like a superhero in my own story, while they're just a bunch of lawyers and car parts. And honestly? I've never felt so empowered. I've been waiting for a chance to call them out, and I finally have. Little did I know, this was just the beginning.
